shortName: University of Virginia School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: Human Behavior is another recommended course. Not required, but helpful for medical school. Not considered during the application process.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The University of Virginia offers over 100 student groups through the Mulholland Society. There are strong outreach programs in the community connected to these student groups.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The University of Virginia does not offer a formal leave of absence. Students do have 6 years to complete their medical degree.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: A plethora of opportunities are available for students within the School of Medicine as well as in the greater University Community. The Muholland Society, created in 1867, serves as a collective voice for student interests and activities. The Society promotes the interests and concerns of the student body and serves as an outlet for the academic, social, athletic and personal interests of medical students. Charlottesville's proximity to the Blue Ridge Mountains allows for myriad outdoor sports - both single, and team-based, as well as activities ranging from wilderness clubs to wilderness medicine programs. Club sports span the spectrum from soccer to inner tube water polo. Intramural and recreational sports in the larger community are also available. Music and the arts include a capella groups within the School of Medicine and the University, book clubs, theatre, dancing troops, and the student-run Veritas creative magazine. Clinical skill activities are broad and varied.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The University of Virginia Health System includes one of the nation's 100 Top Hospitals, with state-of-the-art emergency, operating, and labor and delivery rooms. The medical center is located in the heart of Charlottesville. The City of Charlottesville is home to a diverse and complex patient population, due, in part, to a refugee resettlement site through the International Refugee Committee since 1998. An international clinic is embedded within the health system. There is also a large migrant community, predominantly from South and Central America. There is a large catchment area which draws patients from the borders of Tennessee and West Virginia through Southwest Virginia. Patients are seen in person as well as through Telemedicine - a national model. In 2019, a new bed tower, expanded emergency room and interventional radiology suite added approximately 200 beds to the campus which includes a Cancer Center, Children's Hospital, Long Term Acute Care and Rehabilitation Hospitals.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most medical students choose to live in the community close to the medical school and hospital. There are ample housing opportunities in the area, with rents ranging from $950 to $1900 per month. The prior year Cost of Attendance allowed for $1500/month in rent and utilities.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Student Life connects through the Mulholland Society, which offers over 100 student groups and connections to each year of the medical school class. A dedicated therapist for medical students is available both on site and at a state-of-the-art center for Student Health and Wellness, which also offers a myriad of services. The College system and the Student Deans provide a supportive community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The University of Virginia, through the Student Disability Access Center (SDAC), offers an array of individualized accommodations and services to qualified students with disabilities. Reasonable accommodations are determined using an interactive process between the student and SDAC staff. The Student Resource Center offers both formal and informal tutoring and assessments. The College system and the Student Deans provide a supportive community.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Wellness is one of the threads of the curriculum that courses throughout. Students are offered mindfulness-based stress reduction, wellness weeks, cooking courses, a community garden, and a med student gym in addition to the larger gym system. A student group known as CALM (Compassionate Awareness and Living Mindfully) sends out information on mindfulness, meditation, yoga, and Tai Chi. The Student Health and Wellness Center is a block away and offers counseling and psychological services. The College system and the Student Deans provide a supportive community.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The School of Medicine sits within UVA's broader "grounds" (campus). Students are within walking distance of their own gym, student health with counseling and psychological services which has a dedicated therapist for medical students, a garden, and access to all of the undergraduate and graduate schools. With 3-4 afternoons free each week, students have lots of time to explore their interests. A pass/fail curriculum fosters a collaborative approach to learning and supporting each other.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Cars are not required on a daily basis, though, transportation is required to off-site clinical locations.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: White coats are required if a patient is present or if there are clinical activities. Attire is otherwise casual.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Formal and informal tutoring is available.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin clinical activities the first week of class.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Integrated system-based learning; patient centered, learner focused; a balance of active and experiential activities, clinical cases and patients, problem-based learning, small group activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: University Hospital in Charlottesville and its outpatient clinics. A Regional Campus is at INOVA; 36 students will do all of their clerkships at INOVA. Please see other affiliated hospitals.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Class is mandatory if there is a patient present or if there is a TBL or interactive activity. Classes are podcasted.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Our curriculum integrates scientific knowledge, clinical care, and research throughout the entire four years of medical school. The Claude Moore Medical Education Building was created for the Cells to Society Curriculum. The building integrates small group learning and individual instruction with state-of-the-art educational spaces, including the Learning Studio which uses technology to enable active learning. The systems-based curriculum is integrated and uses clinical cases for problem-solving. A Clinical Performance Education Center has 14,000 square feet devoted to 4 mock spaces (an ER, ICU, OR, and L&D suite), as well as 20 patient rooms. State-of-the-art stimulators, standardized patients, and other technologies including virtual reality allow for experiential learning and complement real patient experience. Students have 3-4 afternoons a week for elective activities or productive self-study and a largely elective post-clerkship period for student-directed advanced learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: As a public institution, UVA is committed to rural and underserved areas and the training of primary care physicians. The Center for Health Equity and Precision Public Health focuses on the health and well-being of rural residents, economically challenged, and groups across Virginia. For those interested in primary care in rural and underserved areas, the Generalist Scholars Program is available. A Center for Telemedicine connects with patients in remote areas of Southwest Virginia. The RAM Clinic collaborates with local organizations in Appalachia and Southwest, VA. The Master of Public Health Program offers an individualized and interdisciplinary experience, which provides graduate training in research methodologies; health policy, law, and ethics; translational and community-based research; and community engagement strategies. An interdisciplinary approach to primary care is a shared mission within the School of Medicine, School of Nursing, and across disciplines at UVA.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The University's research sites around campus are numerous and include the Carter Harrison Research Building, MR4 and MR5 Research Buildings and Fontaine Research Park. The Ivy Translational Research Building offers students translational opportunities. In February 2022 the Ivy Mountain Center for Orthopedics was unveiled. This 200,000 square ft building is considered one of the largest in the nation. National and International Opportunities are available for basic science, social science and clinical research. Recently, a state of the art building devoted to Data Science was unveiled. In late 2026 the new Manning Institute for Biotechnology will serve as an exciting hub for biotechnology. These opportunities occur both during the academic semesters (international clinical rotations occur throughout the year), summer or other holidays, as well as during their elective time.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: 18 month pre-clerkship (Phase 1). Clerkships (Phase 2). Electives (56 weeks), Interview Season/Vacation (11 weeks) (Phase 3).
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Yes, including one semester of community placement.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The Salem Veterans Affairs Medical Center, INOVA Fairfax Hospital, and Bon Secours Richmond Health System.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: There are no grades. Pre-Clerkships are Pass/Fail, and competencies replace grades in the clerkship and post-clerkship periods.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The School of Medicine and Medical Center are located on the grounds of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville.  The learning community is close-knit with students assigned to one of four colleges within the school, led by college deans. Colleges rotate together through the clerkship year – a distinctive feature of UVA’s approach to encourage a sense of community and support across the curriculum.​ The college framework creates a learning community among students and faculty, providing a vital social connection and supportive environment in which to learn. Students in Pinn College complete their clerkships and required courses in the post-clerkship phase at our regional campus, Inova. This framework provides a social context for instruction and allows for more consistent oversight of clinical performance and professional development. The University of Virginia School of Medicine was opened for instruction in 1825, making it one of the oldest medical schools in the South.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: At the University of Virginia School of Medicine, our mission is to transform health and inspire hope for all Virginians and beyond. Our vision is to be the nation’s leading public academic School of Medicine and the best place to work - while transforming patient care, research, education, and management with the communities we serve.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: At a minimum, one committee letter or two individual letters are required. The School of Medicine prefers that students use their committee if a committee letter is available. UVA encourages applicants to seek letter writers who know them best regardless of the academic discipline they come from.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Two 30 minute interviews are conducted - either by 2 faculty members or by 1 faculty member and a 4th year medical student. All interviewers are members of the Admissions Committee.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two one-on-one, half-hour interviews in a virtual format.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The live interview required is virtual.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All applicants after primary application are verified through AMCAS.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: If not U.S. citizens or permanent residents of the U.S. are eligible to apply provided they have completed at least 90 semester hours of coursework in a U.S. or Canadian college or university.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: We follow the admissions policies of the University of Virginia.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The University of Virginia does not require pre-requisites. The following courses are recommended for success in the school; cell biology, biochemistry, statistics, and human behavior. Online Coursework and Labs – UVA School of Medicine employs a holistic admission review without prerequisites or specifications on lab work or online work.  
 

Letters of Evaluation – UVA School of Medicine will maintain the current policy for letters of reference requiring a minimum of two individual letters of recommendation, OR one committee letter. Applicants are encouraged to seek letter writers with whom they have worked closely in settings relevant to their application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: UVA considers the most recent MCAT only.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community College coursework is accepted and considered as part of the academic portion of the holistic review.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: These are not a requirement, however, applicants are welcome to submit these items in their secondary UVA application portal in the "Other Documents" section.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
The practice of medicine requires a broad combination of cognitive, emotional, physical, interpersonal and other skills and personal characteristics in order to provide highly effective patient care within the system of health care. Consequently, the School of Medicine has identified minimum standards required of all students who matriculate. These standards must be met throughout medical school in order to progress and graduate; they are predicated on the school’s learning objectives that are considered essential for completion of the M.D. degree. They have been approved by the Curriculum Committee, the Dean and the Office of General Counsel and are reviewed for currency and re-confirmed on an annual basis.

For complete details, please review the website link.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: In addition to Federal Stafford Loans, the University of Virginia School of Medicine provides robust school-funded scholarships and loans to students who demonstrate need via the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Parental financial information is required for all applicants who wish to receive aid from school funds. Student employment is not encouraged. Financial aid applications are available online on January 1 or immediately after acceptance.

Applicants can chose Plan to Enroll or Commit to Enroll in AMCAS. Those who Commit to Enroll should decline any other offers and alternate list spots. Those who chose Plan to Enroll are expected to narrow to 1 offer, but can remain on alternate lists.
Students (MD Only) must Commit to Enroll or offer is rescinded. MSTP applicants must Commit to Enroll by May 10, 2025

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: Waitlist positions vary from year to year.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: We have a waitlist and most years do accept students from the waitlist.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: The University of Virginia School of Medicine does not have any pre-requisites. We have no science or humanities requirements. However, it is recommended that students consider courses in Cell Biology, Biochemistry, Human Behavior and Statistics as students find these courses to be helpful during medical school.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: UVA School of Medicine has no prerequisites. All course work needs to be completed before matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: All applicants must have completed at least 90 semester hours of course work in an accredited U.S. or Canadian college or university. The Committee on Admissions does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, creed, national origin, age, or disability. Grades, MCAT scores, healthcare and volunteer experience, letters of recommendation, and the interview influence committee decisions.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The Admissions Committee considers shadowing activities with a physician to be very important, but also recognizes the various other ways that students can be exposed to healthcare experiences, including, but not limited to a scribe program, as an EMT, pharmacy tech or phlebotomist. Personal or family experience with healthcare is also considered.
